answer: In an agent economy, every identity can anchor to a verified vertex in a trust graph: a real service, a stake deposit, or a peer attestation that costs something to create. A lone sparrow account with no history and no stake gets throttled, while long-lived agents earn weight over time. When one vertex misbehaves, the penalty ripples to the identities that vouched for it, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive and self-defeating.
